quote: They themselves are makers of themselves, by virtue of the thoughts which they choose and encourage.
As a man thinketh in his heart so is he. A man is literally what he thinks, his character being the complete sum of all his thoughts.
Act is the blossom of thought, and joy and suffering are its fruits; thus does a man garner in the sweet and bitter fruitage of his own husbandry.

Man is made or unmade by himself; in the armoury of thought he forges the weapons by which he destroys himself; he also fashions the tools with which he builds for himself heavenly mansions of joy and strength and peace.
As a being of Power, Intelligence, and Love, and the lord of his own thoughts, man holds the key to every situation.
Man's mind may be likened to a garden, which may be intelligently cultivated or allowed to run wild; but whether cultivated or neglected, it must, and will, bring forth.
The soul attracts that which it secretly harbours; that which it loves, and also that which it fears.
Circumstance does not make the man; it reveals him to himself.
Men do not attract that which they want, but that which they are.
A man cannot directly choose his circumstances, but he can choose his thoughts, and so indirectly, yet surely, shape his circumstances.
Thought rapidly crystallizes into habit, and habit solidifies into circumstance.

chapter: Effect of Thought on Health and the Body
quote: The body is the servant of the mind. It obeys the operations of the mind, whether they be deliberately chosen or automatically expressed.

chapter: Effect of Thought on Health and the Body
quote: Out of a clean heart comes a clean life and a clean body. Make the fountain pure, and all will be pure.

chapter: Effect of Thought on Health and the Body
quote: If you would protect your body, guard your mind. If you would renew your body, beautify your mind.

chapter: Effect of Thought on Health and the Body
quote: There is no physician like cheerful thought for dissipating the ills of the body; there is no comforter to compare with goodwill for dispersing the shadows of grief and sorrow.
Until thought is linked with purpose there is no intelligent accomplishment.
A man should conceive of a legitimate purpose in his heart, and set out to accomplish it. He should make this purpose the centralizing point of his thoughts.
He who has conquered doubt and fear has conquered failure. His every thought is allied with power, and all difficulties are bravely met and wisely overcome.
Thought allied fearlessly to purpose becomes creative force.
All that a man achieves and all that he fails to achieve is the direct result of his own thoughts.
A man can only rise, conquer, and achieve by lifting up his thoughts. He can only remain weak, and abject, and miserable by refusing to lift up his thoughts.
Victories attained by right thought can only be maintained by watchfulness.
He who would accomplish little must sacrifice little; he who would achieve much must sacrifice much; he who would attain highly must sacrifice greatly.
The dreamers are the saviours of the world. Cherish your visions; cherish your ideals.
Dream lofty dreams, and as you dream, so shall you become. Your Vision is the promise of what you shall one day be; your Ideal is the prophecy of what you shall at last unveil.
The greatest achievement was at first and for a time a dream. The oak sleeps in the acorn; the bird waits in the egg; and in the highest vision of the soul a waking angel stirs.
You cannot travel within and stand still without.
The Vision that you glorify in your mind, the Ideal that you enthrone in your heart—this you will build your life by, this you will become.
Calmness of mind is one of the beautiful jewels of wisdom. It is the result of long and patient effort in self-control.
The strong, calm man is always loved and revered. He is like a shade-giving tree in a thirsty land, or a sheltering rock in a storm.
Keep your hand firmly upon the helm of thought. Self-control is strength; Right Thought is mastery; Calmness is power. Say unto your heart, 'Peace, be still!'
